subject: marathon runners
one_liner: Every mile is a task. Every task has an assignee. The assignee is your left leg, and it is behind.
brand_voice_notes: Work-management SaaS sincerity applied to a 42.195 km run. The product treats the body as a cross-functional team (Left Leg, Right Leg, Lungs, Morale) that keeps missing deadlines. Never jokes about running being hard. Talks about it like a Q3 roadmap slipping.

hero.sub: Taper breaks your marathon into mile-level work items, assigns each one to a body part, and escalates when Morale misses a standup. The finish line is now a deliverable.

features.title: Mile-level task assignment
features.blurb: Each mile is a ticket with an owner, a due pace and dependencies. Mile 14 is blocked by Mile 13. We did not make the rule. We made it visible.

features.title: Aid-station standups
features.blurb: A 90-second async standup at every water table. What did you run, what will you run, what is blocking you. Most runners write 'hamstring'. We file it.

features.title: Toenail portfolio view
features.blurb: Ten toenails, ten projects, one status board. On Track, At Risk, Off Track and Detached. Finance gets a weekly digest.

demo_screen_concept: A race-day kanban board for the 2026 Lakeshore Marathon: 27 mile-task cards (Mile 1 to Mile 26 plus 'The .2') across Backlog, Running, Blocked and Done columns. Each card shows an assignee chip (Left Leg, Right Leg, Lungs, Morale), a target split, and a dependency count. Filter chips by assignee, a 'Complete mile' button that moves the current card to Done and advances a race clock and progress bar, a 'Log blocker' modal (chafing, side stitch, saw a dog, emotional) that moves the current card to Blocked, and a toenail portfolio sidebar with ten status pills that cycle on click.

design_direction.style: Kinetic sports editorial, asphalt night-run mode. A work-management SaaS dressed as a night-race shoe campaign: wet asphalt ground, volt-yellow and race-orange as the only bright colours, extra-condensed uppercase display type set huge and tight, slanted motion, monospace race-clock numerals. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: trail signs, blazes, contour lines, label tape, crossed-out names, middle slots, fridge magnets, ghost text, keycaps, squiggles, chrome bubbles, read receipts, sale-bill stacks, lot boxes, manicules, misregistration, activity rings, waveforms, readout chips, collar bands, aisle signs, shelf tags, pallet beams, member cards, scorecard grids, stitch seams, pencil notes, pennants. Also absent: daylight backgrounds, serif type, glassmorphism, blur, paper textures, handwriting, rounded corners above 4px. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The race bib: features, tiers and testimonials sit on off-white Tyvek bib cards with a big bib number, four punched safety-pin holes in the corners and a perforated tear-off strip. (2) The split clock: every number reads like a finish-line clock (HH:MM:SS, tabular mono, volt on black). (3) The pace line: a dashed volt racing line with mile-marker ticks runs between sections and under the hero. (4) The motion slant: headlines and the primary CTA are skewed -8deg, like they left before the gun.

fonts.body: 'Work Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

design_direction.archetype: Product-led SaaS landing (hero, feature bibs, social proof, pricing), with the demo as a kanban work-management board
design_direction.motion_vocab: Horizontal motion only. Pace-line dashes march left on a slow loop; the race clock ticks; bibs slide in from the right with a 40ms stagger on reveal, gated on a .js class with a timeout fallback. All motion off under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Left: giant skewed three-line H1 in Big Shoulders 900, volt on the word 'Zero'. Right: night-run hero photo, with a live split clock overlaid at its bottom edge. Pace line with mile ticks runs full-bleed under the hero.

images.rationale: Shoe-campaign style direction wants a photographic hero, so one hero. Demo is a kanban board, not photo-shaped, so no demo assets. Remaining budget of 3 went to deadpan headshots for all three testimonials.

items.prompt: Editorial sports photograph, night marathon: a single runner mid-stride on wet black asphalt city street at night, low side angle, sodium streetlights, hard rim light. Charcoal #141619 dominant, volt #D7FF3D vest, race orange #FF5A1F cone. Cinematic shoe-campaign mood, grainy film. Correction appended on attempt 2: all clothing and shoes plain and unbranded, no swooshes, no race bib. No text, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks or UI.
